active_paradigms.idea: Replace the destination-only Steiner MILP with a partition-aware capacitated directed-Steiner MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program solves a directed edge-installation Steiner formulation: one binary variable per edge is charged once and one continuous commodity per unique destination proves source reachability. This is strong when the evaluator charges a relay edge only once regardless of the number of receivers, and it correctly exploits common prefixes of destination routes. However, it assigns every partition of every destination to the identical path and does not impose throughput constraints or model simultaneous traffic at all. The supplied evaluator wrapper only serializes calls and delegates to an unavailable evaluator.py, so its actual cost aggregation and capacity validation cannot be inferred from the shown code; this must be aligned with the delegate's semantics. Formulate binary path-use variables per (destination, partition, edge), binary installation variables per edge, flow conservation for each partition demand, and an edge-capacity constraint summing simultaneous partition traffic on each edge. Charge installation variables once only if evaluator cost is deduplicated across the topology; otherwise charge partition-edge variables with the evaluator's actual partition data fraction. Use the existing scipy.optimize.milp call directly with a short, deterministic time limit and retain only a feasible incumbent whose selected variables can be decomposed into simple source-to-destination paths. This can improve over the current solution specifically when parallel partitions must be distributed over multiple links to avoid throughput penalties or infeasible overloaded edges.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The primary scalar score under the evaluator's true aggregation rule, especially any throughput/capacity feasibility term, transfer-completion penalty, and redundant-transfer cost caused by sending all partitions through one path.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not assume the current shared-edge objective is correct merely because it is a good heuristic: inspect the delegated evaluator before deciding whether an edge is charged once, once per destination, or once per partition. Scale partition demands consistently with the graph's throughput units, and reject fractional routing if BroadCastTopology requires one discrete edge list per partition. Avoid the current 90-second worst-case model if the evaluation has a tighter hidden timeout; reduce variables by omitting unreachable destination-partitions and unusable edges.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a rooted minimum directed arborescence via networkx.minimum_spanning_arborescence when the evaluator rewards one broadcast tree
active_paradigms.description: The present exact model is a directed Steiner-tree solver, but its commodity formulation has O(number of destinations times number of edges) continuous variables and can become slow or fail to return an incumbent. A rooted directed arborescence is a structurally valid broadcast topology: every retained receiver has one unambiguous source path and each relay edge is naturally shared by all descendants. Construct the optimization graph from only nodes and edges permitted by the evaluator, add a synthetic root with a zero-cost edge only to src, and call networkx.minimum_spanning_arborescence on this rooted graph. Remove the synthetic root edge, discard branches with no requested destination descendant, and assign each destination its unique arborescence path for all partitions when capacity is not part of scoring. The current program's strengths are its valid directed paths, removal of invalid costs, and shared-prefix accounting; preserve those sanitization rules before invoking the arborescence routine. This is fundamentally faster and more deterministic than a MILP and can beat the incumbent on instances where HiGHS times out or returns a weak feasible Steiner solution. It is most appropriate if the cloud graph is small/dense and the evaluator charges unique selected broadcast edges rather than individual packet copies.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Shared-link transfer cost and evaluator consistency through a single acyclic directed broadcast structure, while eliminating MILP timeout variability.
active_paradigms.cautions: A minimum arborescence spans every node supplied to it, not just requested terminals, so supplying the entire graph can add expensive irrelevant branches and be worse than Steiner. Restrict the input vertex set to an evaluator-justified candidate subgraph before the single arborescence call, and ensure src is the only possible root using the synthetic-root construction. This approach does not itself handle per-edge simultaneous-flow capacities or multiple paths per partition.

active_paradigms.idea: Model independent partition traffic as a capacitated min-cost flow with networkx.min_cost_flow
active_paradigms.description: The current algorithm assumes multicast replication is free after an edge has been installed, which is optimal only under a topology-level shared-edge billing model. If the hidden evaluator instead adds cost or load for each partition traversal, the relevant problem is a capacitated transportation flow problem rather than directed Steiner tree. Build a flow graph whose source has supply equal to total partition demand, each destination has demand equal to its number of partitions, edge capacities are derived from throughput over the evaluator's transfer interval, and edge weights equal the evaluator's per-unit data-transfer price. Call networkx.min_cost_flow once to obtain an integral minimum-cost aggregate routing under those capacities. Decompose each positive source-to-destination flow unit into one simple path and place those paths in the corresponding destination partition slots, allowing partitions for the same receiver to use different routes. This directly realizes the stated objective of balancing traffic across parallel cloud networks and avoids the current design's systematic oversubscription of a single cheap bottleneck. It is a particularly good alternative when costs are per GB per traversal and link throughput is a hard constraint rather than a negligible tie-breaker.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total per-partition transfer price subject to link capacities, plus any evaluator penalties for oversubscribed links or poor use of parallel network paths.
active_paradigms.cautions: This deliberately does not obtain free shared-edge multicast discounts: use it only when evaluator accounting is flow-additive or capacity penalties outweigh broadcast sharing. NetworkX min_cost_flow requires integer capacities, demands, and weights, so multiply floating costs and throughput-derived capacities by a fixed safe scale and round consistently. Positive aggregate flow must be decomposed without creating cycles, and each emitted BroadCastTopology path must retain the original G edge-data dictionaries expected by the evaluator.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the size-limited Steiner DP with an exact directed-Steiner MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program constructs a directed shared multicast tree: for at most 13 unique receivers it uses the classical subset dynamic program with merge states and reverse Dijkstra, then falls back to a greedy shortest attachment tree. This is strong because each selected edge is shared by all downstream destinations, but the 13-terminal cutoff means larger cases can be substantially suboptimal, and neither branch models link throughput or partition-level congestion. Formulate a directed Steiner arborescence as a mixed-integer linear program with binary edge-installation variables y_e and one unit of commodity flow f_(terminal,e) for every destination terminal. Require every terminal commodity to send one unit from src to that terminal, constrain f_(t,e) <= y_e, and minimize sum(cost_e * y_e), optionally adding a very small tie-breaker based on inverse throughput or hop count. This directly solves the same shared-edge cost model that the current DP optimizes, but without exponential subset enumeration and without a heuristic cutoff. After solving, retain edges with y_e near one, extract a src-to-dst path in the selected subgraph, and assign that valid path to each partition. If evaluation actually charges congestion or transfer duration, extend the model with partition/commodity flow variables and capacity constraints rather than assuming the same route can carry every partition simultaneously.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary shared data-transfer cost, especially instances with more than 13 receivers where the present greedy fallback is not globally optimal; secondarily use throughput as a tie-breaker or explicit feasibility constraint.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The supplied wrapper exposes no evaluator internals beyond calling evaluator.py, so its exact aggregation of partition cost and throughput cannot be proven from the shown code. Only include finite-cost edges, remove incoming edges to src, and add a practical time limit because multi-commodity MILPs grow as terminals times edges. Ensure every destination has a graph path before adding equality-demand constraints; handle unreachable destinations consistently with evaluator expectations. Do not mistake a fractional LP solution for a topology: y_e must be integral and selected paths must be reconstructed from the integer solution.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use NetworkX network_simplex on a partition-expanded capacitated flow graph to route partitions over different networks
tried_paradigms.description: The existing algorithm gives every partition of every destination exactly the same tree path, so it receives sharing but completely ignores the stated goal of parallel paths and the throughput fields in G. Build a partition-expanded directed graph in which each data partition is represented as one demand unit, edge capacities are derived from throughput, and per-edge cost is the evaluator-relevant transferred-byte cost. Add node/edge copies or capacity gadgets so a physical link has one aggregate capacity across all partition commodities, while each destination-partition has a required delivery demand. Invoke networkx.network_simplex once to obtain a minimum-cost feasible integral flow, then decompose each delivered unit of flow into src-to-destination paths for BroadCastTopology. This is fundamentally different from choosing a single multicast tree: it deliberately splits partitions across parallel cheap links and prevents all partitions from oversubscribing the same bottleneck. It should be particularly valuable if the evaluator computes transfer time from edge flow divided by throughput, or rejects/penalizes flows exceeding edge throughput. A sharing discount can be approximately represented by adding a low-cost first-use capacity tier and higher-cost subsequent capacity tiers for each physical edge, provided that matches the actual evaluator's billing semantics.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Partition-level load balance, edge-capacity feasibility, and elapsed transfer time while minimizing total routed transfer cost.
tried_paradigms.cautions: network_simplex is single-commodity, so a plain construction can accidentally permit flow intended for one destination to satisfy another; destination-specific sink layers or a super-sink construction must preserve destination demands before path decomposition. NetworkX demands use a sign convention: source supply is negative and sink demand is positive. Integer capacities must be scaled carefully from floating throughput, and zero/negative-cost cycles should be avoided. This model is preferable only when evaluator bills each partition transfer or models congestion; if it bills a physical multicast edge once regardless of downstream copies, the MILP/Steiner formulation is more faithful.

tried_paradigms.idea: Generate throughput-diverse candidate routes with NetworkX shortest_simple_paths and assign partitions to distinct path families
tried_paradigms.description: The current exact DP has an excellent sharing objective but is blind to alternative near-cost routes: it normally emits one path to each receiver and clones it to all partitions. For every destination, use networkx.shortest_simple_paths on a scalarized edge weight that preserves monetary cost as the dominant term while using a tiny inverse-throughput or congestion tie-breaker. Consume only a small bounded prefix of simple paths, discard candidates containing missing-cost edges, and classify candidates by their first expensive inter-cloud edge or by physical-edge overlap. Assign partitions round-robin or by current accumulated normalized load across the least-overlapping low-cost candidates, while retaining the common Steiner prefix whenever its edge is genuinely cheaper than duplicate source egress. This supplies actual parallelism without changing BroadCastTopology's expected per-destination/per-partition path representation. It is also a useful robust alternative if the evaluator measures a makespan-like completion time, since routing all partitions identically can make one low-throughput edge dominate despite its low dollar cost. Use the current Steiner-tree route as an always-available baseline candidate, and only select a divergent candidate when its evaluator-aligned cost/time estimate is better.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Avoid redundant use of a bottleneck by distributing partitions over low-cost, edge-disjoint or low-overlap routes; improve throughput utilization with minimal increase in monetary cost.
tried_paradigms.cautions: shortest_simple_paths is a generator whose worst-case runtime can be large, so stop after a fixed small number of candidates per destination and avoid requesting paths for unreachable nodes. It does not itself perform the final assignment; the crucial policy is to track aggregate load per physical edge and reject candidates that would exceed throughput. A naive cost perturbation can change genuinely optimal cost paths, so keep the throughput term lexicographically tiny or first restrict candidates to a tight cost band. If evaluator counts shared edges only once, excessive path diversity can increase cost and should be used only where capacity pressure justifies it.
